explanation: Its relatives include horseradish and mustard. Their heat comes from vapours that rise into the nose, unlike chilli heat, which burns the tongue and lingers.

claims.text: Wasabi (Eutrema japonicum) belongs to the cabbage family, Brassicaceae, and is prepared by grating its rhizome, a thick stem.
Wasabi is not a member of the ginger, onion or mint family.
Horseradish and mustard are also members of the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.
The pungency of wasabi, horseradish and mustard is caused by volatile isothiocyanates that rise into the nasal passages.
Chilli heat, by contrast, is felt in the mouth and lasts longer.

evidence.restatement: Wasabi, Eutrema japonicum, is in the cabbage family, and its rhizome, a thick stem, is what is grated.
Wasabi is not in the ginger, onion or mint family.
Horseradish and mustard are also Brassicaceae.
Their pungency comes from volatile isothiocyanates, such as allyl isothiocyanate, which reach the nose.
Capsaicin is not volatile, so chilli heat stays in the mouth and lingers longer.
Wasabi (Eutrema japonicum) is in the cabbage or mustard family, Brassicaceae; the part grated is the rhizome, a thick underground stem.

The pungency of these plants comes from volatile isothiocyanates that reach the nasal passages.
